fileName: 35 - Catching the Pullback with VWAP, LRCs and Forks.mkv
displayTitle: Catching the Pullback with VWAP, LRCs and Forks

content.fullText: [00:01] In this lesson, we will use the fractal price action reading framework with the aid of an anchored VWAP tool, which is another great tool from volume analysis that acts as a dynamic fractal barrier. The VWAP is unique in the sense that it merges the geometric and numerical elements of an indicator at the same time it incorporates the element of volume. Let's begin by performing some phase analysis on this market. We see now that price is retracing against an upward price movement. So, we should be able to find an Elliot wave pattern in the impulsive part and on the retracing part of price action in order to validate the beginning of the next impulsive movement or not. In this next chart, you can see an example of Elliot wave reading where a clear five and three-wave patterns are identified. More importantly, within the ABC pattern of the current reversal, we can find five waves in a smaller degree of the C-wave. That is the first indication that this retracement might be near its end. If we erase this Elliot wave reading, which can get confusing very rapidly, and simply plot a Fibonacci retracement tool from the lowest low to the highest high, we'll observe that price is now landing on the very common and very widely observed 61.8% ratio. Notice that in the case of tools like Fibonacci, the self-fulfilling prophecy effect is more prominent in the more obvious ratios. The 61.8% is very common, along with the 100, 200, 161.8, and 261.8% ratios. One additional detail about this 61.8% level is that it correlates with a resistance level that is now being tested as support. In terms of the Dow Theory, this market is in an uptrend in the broader sense. And in the minor sense, it's in a downtrend since it's producing lower highs and lower lows. If we integrate Elliot with Dow here, we'll arrive at the conclusion that Elliot is providing a leading signal to the Dow Theory, since it points to the termination of the retracement. In terms of overextension, we cannot find bullish signals in terms of volume, and we cannot find velocity reversal divergences in the RSI. But we can find a velocity reversal divergence in the ultimate oscillator, as you can see here. The ultimate oscillator was developed by Larry Williams and it provides a different perspective in terms of oscillators. The point here is that different oscillators will point to divergences in different areas. So just because you don't see a divergence in the RSI, it doesn't mean that there is no other type of divergence happening in other technical indicators. In terms of price barriers beyond the Fib retracement level that we already found, we can see two pitchforks that point to the current price action as a market edge. There's a third pitchfork we can draw in the really small highs and lows, and this fork will point to the same interpretation. Notice that as we integrate all these signals, the likelihood that price will reverse at this point because of a great coincidence starts to decrease very rapidly. A simple trading channel here will also point to the same interpretation of the pitchforks. Still in terms of barriers, we can draw a linear regression channel to capture the statistical stability of this market from this low to the current price action, which has the potential of being another low. Notice how we have symmetrical overthrows that increase the accuracy of the interpretation. A second linear regression channel can be drawn, but this time using a major high as the first grounding position. Observe that we have a similar occurrence with the overthrows. As a final barrier, we can plot an anchored VWAP tool in the lowest low of the chart. And you will see that the center VWAP line is cutting through the lower shadow of the current candle, highlighting yet another intersection. Notice the strength of the barriers involved: a strong self-fulfilling Fibonacci level, three pitchforks, two linear regression channels, and a major VWAP line. Integrating that with the perspective given by phase analysis, we can say that this is a moment when analyzing candlesticks more closely is appropriate. Notice that in this case, price creates a DFP to the upside, and it goes from a downward progression immediately to an upward progression, and it displays no fractal candles. That serves to show that not all reversals occur with fractal candles. We have a bias change with an increase in body size demonstrating an increase in power from buyers. This is the signal to get in a long trade at this point, given the overall context provided by the fractal price action reading framework. In this next chart, you can see how this was indeed a market edge and price moved significantly to the upside after that. In this final chart, you can see how a modified shift pitchfork grounded on the major market extremes would provide a secondary entry level and point to the peak of the market that followed.

keyEvents.description: A candlestick chart is shown, displaying a clear uptrend followed by a corrective pullback. The asset is Australian Dollar vs. Canadian Dollar (AUD/CAD) on a 45-minute timeframe.

Elliot Wave theory labels are overlaid on the chart. An impulsive 5-wave structure (labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) is marked on the uptrend, with sub-waves shown inside waves 3 and 5. A corrective ABC structure is marked on the pullback, with a smaller 5-wave structure detailed within the final C-wave.

The Elliot Wave labels are removed. A Fibonacci retracement tool is drawn from the absolute low of the uptrend to the absolute high. The 0.618 (61.8%) level is shown, with the price currently reacting to this specific level.

Two oscillator indicators are added below the main price chart: the Ultimate Oscillator (UO, red line) and the Relative Strength Index (RSI, black line). Lines are drawn on the price chart (connecting two lower lows) and on the oscillators (connecting the corresponding lows). A clear bullish divergence is shown on both oscillators, where the indicator makes a higher low while price makes a lower low.

The oscillators are removed. Two blue Andrews' Pitchforks are drawn. The first is drawn on the larger swing, capturing the entire pullback. The second is drawn on a smaller, more recent swing within the pullback.
The previous pitchforks are removed, and a third, smaller, red-colored pitchfork is drawn on the most recent downward price move.
The pitchfork is replaced by a simple parallel channel (trading channel) drawn by connecting the recent highs and lows of the pullback.

The parallel channel is replaced by a Linear Regression Channel, highlighted in a blue shaded area. The tool is anchored from a low point before the final peak and extends to the current price, showing price hitting the lower boundary.
A second, smaller Linear Regression Channel is overlaid, anchored from the absolute market high, showing a confluence of boundaries at the current price.

An Anchored VWAP (Volume-Weighted Average Price) tool is plotted, originating from the absolute low of the entire uptrend. The blue center VWAP line is shown intersecting with the low of the current candlestick, indicating a dynamic support level.

The chart progresses forward in time, showing that the identified confluence point was indeed the bottom of the pullback. A significant upward price move follows. A green arrow is placed at the reversal point, labeled as the market edge.

A final chart shows the entire price move. A red-colored Modified Schiff Pitchfork is drawn using the major swing points (low-high-low) of the entire trend. The pitchfork's median line and parallel lines are shown to have effectively contained the subsequent price action, identifying a secondary entry and the eventual market top.

semanticAnalysis.mainConcept: The core lesson is about achieving a high-probability trade setup through the principle of confluence, which is termed 'hyper-integration'. It demonstrates a systematic process of layering multiple, independent technical analysis tools—Elliot Wave for phase analysis, Fibonacci for numerical targets, oscillators for momentum divergence, and various geometric tools (Pitchforks, Channels, VWAP) for identifying dynamic barriers. The convergence of all these distinct analytical methods at a single price point creates a 'market edge,' significantly increasing the probability that a pullback is ending and the primary trend will resume.
semanticAnalysis.deeperMeaning: The underlying philosophy is that no single indicator or trading method is reliable on its own. True market insight comes from a holistic, multi-perspective analysis where geometric structure, numerical relationships, momentum, and volume-based levels align. This approach is designed to reduce ambiguity and filter out low-quality signals. It implies that a trader's confidence and success rate are proportional to the number of non-correlated analytical reasons supporting a trade idea. The reference to 'self-fulfilling prophecy' also suggests an awareness of market psychology and how widely-used tools can influence price action.
semanticAnalysis.educationalGoal: The educational objective is to teach students how to build a robust, evidence-based case for entering a trade, specifically focusing on buying a pullback within an established uptrend. This lesson serves as a practical application of the 'Fractal Price Action Reading Framework' by integrating diverse concepts into a single, coherent trading decision. It aims to elevate the student's analysis from basic signal-following to a sophisticated, contextual understanding of market dynamics, thereby fostering more disciplined and high-conviction trading.
